Definition: a mass of persons (or figuratively, things), especially reg. organized for war (an army); by implication, a campaign, literally or figuratively (specifically, hardship, worship)
BiblicalUsage: Tsaba is a host — an army, a company under command. Genesis says the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them; Joshua met the captain of the host of the LORD outside Jericho; and David walked out to Goliath in the name of the LORD of hosts. The same word covers the stars, the angels, and the armies of Israel, because all of them serve under one Commander.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe 'the LORD of hosts' is one of the greatest names of God in Scripture — He commands every army in heaven and on earth. My position is that no enemy is too great when the LORD of hosts fights for His people, and no battle is too small for Him to care about. The God who made the host of heaven is the God who stands with His people.
